newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank shares rise in heavy demand.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank shares rise in heavy demand.

text.p: All three bank shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange continued to rise on Monday amid heavy demand, high turnover and continued investor excitement over newcomer Bank of Beirut.

Banque Audi rose to $19.625 from $19.5, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $14.75 from $14.5 and Bank of Beirut reached $3.125 from Friday's opening trading price of $3 which was 38 percent above its $2.17 issue price.
Market volume was $3,287,461 led by Banque Audi with a volume of $1,631,512 on turnover of 83,413 shares including a block trade of 10,975 at $19.125.on the exchange floor.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.17 percent to 125.92 and the two general indexes, the LISPI and BLOM Stock Index rose 0.59 percent and 0.07 percent respectively to 85.43 and 909.28.
Some 3,500 BLC shares changed hands at $14.5 in a block trade on the floor.
Demand for BoB totalled 3,153,158 shares compared with 6.5 million on Friday. Supply was 134,928, all of which were sold.
Some brokers expressed concern about the rapid rise of BoB's shares but the bank said this was unwarranted and they were finding their true market level.
"Bank of Beirut is facing incredible demand. It's unrealistic. It's unrelated to fundamentals," a broker who asked not to be identified told Reuters. "This excitement over BoB is not justified."

Bank of Beirut Chairman Salim Sfeir said the criticism was unjustified: "It's a question of supply and demand, and let the market decide on the value of the share," he told Reuters. "It's very normal after the oversubscription of the private placement that there is demand left," he added.
BoB's $10.4 million private share placement last month was 11 times oversubscribed, leaving many would-be investors scrambling to pick up shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange.
Sfeir said BoB's fundamentals were excellent. "Very shortly we will publish our first quarter earnings and they will show excellent results," he said.
Solidere A and B shares held steady at $10.25 and $10.75 respectively. Turnover was 103,772 shares, nearly three times Friday's 34,796.
Industrial pipemaker Eternit was unchanged at $2 with 12,030 shares changing hands. There was no trade in the other three industrial shares, Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
